definitions: Work over characteristic zero in the original positive-Serre presentation of A(r,s), for all positive integral r,s. Let P=L(V) be the actual pre-Serre positive Lie algebra in the accepted maximal local algebra and I its entire positive Serre ideal; S=P/I. E=ad(e_3), F=ad(f_3), H=ad(h_3). For a formal homogeneous degree alpha=(a,b,n), set m=2n-r a-s b. The ideal I is stable under E,F and the finite-Levi actions, with the actual low-degree Cartan terms retained. Formal grading is used even when Cartan weights coincide.

all_range_root_string_theorem.claim: On the actual homogeneous S_alpha, if m>0 then ker F=0. If m=-d<=0, where d is a nonnegative integer, then ker F equals ker E^(d+1) as subspaces of S_alpha. The latter map lands in the FULL actual S_(a,b,n+d+1), not a lowest subspace and not a free target. At d=0 this reads ker F=ker E; the common space is a direct sum of trivial root-3 sl2 modules.
proof: E is locally nilpotent on the full original Chevalley-Serre algebra: it is nilpotent on each Chevalley generator by the positive Serre relations, and on Cartan and negative generators by the Chevalley brackets; Leibniz extends this to every finite Lie word. By the negative Serre relations and the same argument, F is also locally nilpotent. The triple E,F,H obeys the ordinary sl2 relations.

For any homogeneous x of H-weight m, the sl2 submodule generated by x is finite-dimensional. Indeed the sl2 PBW spanning words can be ordered E^i H^j F^k x. Only finitely many k occur by local nilpotence of F; H acts on F^k x by the scalar m-2k; for each such k, E^i F^k x eventually vanishes. Thus the span is finite. Characteristic-zero finite-dimensional sl2 complete reducibility applies.

In an irreducible highest-weight ell module, the weight -d occurs only when ell>=d with ell congruent to d modulo 2. At that weight F kills exactly the copy with ell=d. The number of E-steps from weight -d to the highest line is (ell+d)/2, so E^(d+1) kills that weight precisely when ell=d as well. This proves equality of kernels on every summand, hence on their direct sum. For m>0 no occurring weight-m vector is lowest in a finite-dimensional sl2 module, so ker F is zero. No positive form or nondegenerate form on g_S is assumed.

precise_original_kernel_reformulation.statement: Fix any actual original root degree alpha=(a,b,n), n>=2, in the ORIGINAL full Serre quotient, and take the true finite-Levi-lowest subspace U_alpha={x in S_alpha : ad(f_1)x=ad(f_2)x=0}. If m=-d<=0, its ordinary critical kernel ker(ad(f_3)) intersect U_alpha is exactly U_alpha intersect ker((ad e_3)^(d+1)). If m>0 it is zero. This holds for ALL positive r,s and for each of the eight original n=5 types, not just a selected root or parameter.
precise_original_kernel_reformulation.free_ideal_presentation: For m=-d<=0 put P_alpha=P intersect the formal alpha component, I_alpha=I intersect P_alpha, and Ufree_alpha={x in P_alpha : [f_1,x] and [f_2,x] lie in I}. The ordinary original kernel is canonically (Ufree_alpha intersect {x in P_alpha : E^(d+1)x lies in I}) / I_alpha. The second I is its full actual homogeneous component at degree (a,b,n+d+1). I_alpha lies in the numerator by ideal stability. This is exact positive-string ideal SATURATION, not a claim the numerator is I_alpha.
precise_original_kernel_reformulation.verification_and_limits: The equality follows by applying the theorem inside the actual original quotient; finite-Levi lowering conditions are imposed only at the original alpha, and the E-string target is the entire actual higher-level quotient. There is no assumption that E commutes with the finite-Levi lowering, no replacement of the higher ideal by its degree-five truncation, and no dimensional or rank inference. For n=5, the established exact Q1/Q2 comparison says this kernel is zero iff BOTH original obstruction multiplicities vanish. The equivalence does not itself show saturation or give a witness.

constructive_strict_chamber_descent.claim: For any homogeneous x in P_alpha with a,b nonnegative, n>=2 and m=2n-r a-s b>0, if [f_3,x] lies in I then x lies in I. This is an explicit ideal-level proof, not merely a quotient-dimension inference; it applies to every vector in the fixed root space, not only lowest vectors.
proof: Let N=r a+s b+1. Express x as a finite sum of positive Chevalley Lie words with a letters e_1, b letters e_2 and n letters e_3; this is the actual formal homogeneous component. Applying E^N by the iterated derivation rule distributes N actions among those factors. A term either hits an e_3 (where E e_3=0), or, by the pigeonhole bound N>r a+s b, applies E at least r+1 times to an e_1 or at least s+1 times to an e_2. Those factors are the defining positive Serre seeds, hence every term lies in the FULL ideal I. Consequently E^N x lies in I. No word enumeration or executed probe is used.

For each k>=1, the exact sl2 commutator identity in the pre-Serre algebra is k(m+k-1) E^(k-1)x = E^k F x - F E^k x. Starting at k=N, both right-hand terms belong to I: F x does by hypothesis, E^N x by the previous paragraph, and I is stable under E and F. Since m>0, the characteristic-zero scalar k(m+k-1) is nonzero, proving E^(N-1)x in I. Descend successively through k=N-1,...,1 to obtain x in I. The same finite identities describe the ideal correction without assuming I is a direct sum of its Serre-descendant terms.
At m=0 the same descent stops with E x in I: the k=1 scalar vanishes. It does not prove x in I. This matches the exact boundary ker F=ker E and prevents a spurious equality-case exclusion.
